q: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities are called _____ quantities.
e: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities are called scalar quantities. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: Quantities that have both magnitude and direction are called _____ quantities.
e: Quantities that have both magnitude and direction are called vector quantities. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: In printing, vectors are represented by _____ type, such as $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{s}$.
e: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type, such as $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{s}$. The physics in this sentence is built around boldface.

q: In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing _____ on the top of their symbols.
e: In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing arrows on the top of their symbols. The physics in this sentence is built around arrows.

q: The magnitude of a vector $\vec{F}$ is written as _____.
e: The magnitude of a vector $\vec{F}$ is written as $F = |\vec{F}|$. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: If $\vec{A} = -\vec{B}$, it means $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are equal in magnitude but have _____ directions.
e: If $\vec{A} = -\vec{B}$, it means $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are equal in magnitude but have opposite directions. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite. Same: lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: If $\vec{A} = 2\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is two times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is _____ that of $\vec{B}$.
e: If $\vec{A} = 2\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is two times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is the same as that of $\vec{B}$. The same as here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: If $\vec{A} = -3\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is three times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is _____ to that of $\vec{B}$.
e: If $\vec{A} = -3\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is three times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is opposite to that of $\vec{B}$. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite. The same as: lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: Using graphical method, the length of the arrow representing a vector is _____ to the magnitude of the vector.
e: Using graphical method, the length of the arrow representing a vector is proportional to the magnitude of the vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: To add $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, first draw $\vec{A}$. Then draw $\vec{B}$ in such a way that the _____ of $\vec{B}$ is at the tip of $\vec{A}$.
e: To add $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, first draw $\vec{A}$. Then draw $\vec{B}$ in such a way that the tail of $\vec{B}$ is at the tip of $\vec{A}$. The physics in this sentence is built around tail.

q: The vector sum $\vec{A} + \vec{B}$ is called the _____ vector.
e: The vector sum $\vec{A} + \vec{B}$ is called the resultant vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Vector addition is _____.
e: Vector addition is commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction. non-commutative is the opposite class from commutative.

q: In algebraic notation, vector subtraction is expressed as $\vec{A} - \vec{B} =$ _____.
e: In algebraic notation, vector subtraction is expressed as $\vec{A} - \vec{B} =$ $\vec{A} + (-\vec{B})$. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Vector subtraction is _____.
e: Vector subtraction is not commutative. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called _____ of a vector.
e: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called resolution of a vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: The new vectors obtained from the resolution of a vector are called vector _____ of the original vector.
e: The new vectors obtained from the resolution of a vector are called vector components of the original vector. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two perpendicular components, namely, _____ component and _____ component.
e: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two perpendicular components, namely, horizontal component and vertical component. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction. Scalar and vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the x-component is given by _____.
e: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the x-component is given by $A_x = A \cos \theta$. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the y-component is given by _____.
e: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the y-component is given by $A_y = A \sin \theta$. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Distance travelled by the body is the _____ of the path along which the body moves.
e: Distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body moves. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start. Displacement: the straight directed change from start point to end point.

q: Displacement is the distance travelled along a _____.
e: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start. Curved path: a bent path, which light does not take in a uniform medium.

q: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a scalar. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a vector. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.

q: The average speed, $v_{av}$, is the ratio of total distance $s$ to _____.
e: The average speed, $v_{av}$, is the ratio of total distance $s$ to time taken $t$. Time taken $t$ here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Displacement: the straight directed change from start point to end point.

q: The average velocity, $\vec{v}_{av}$, is the ratio of total displacement $\vec{s}$ to _____.
e: The average velocity, $\vec{v}_{av}$, is the ratio of total displacement $\vec{s}$ to time taken $t$. Time taken $t$ here means the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force. Total distance $s$: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is _____.
e: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is zero. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as _____ speed and _____ velocity.
e: The speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as instantaneous speed and instantaneous velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Instantaneous speed is defined as the limiting value of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as time $\Delta t$ approaches _____.
e: Instantaneous speed is defined as the limiting value of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as time $\Delta t$ approaches zero. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Distance: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: Motion with constant velocity is known as _____ motion.
e: Motion with constant velocity is known as uniform motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity involving velocity.

q: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an _____.
e: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an acceleration. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes.

q: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} =$ _____.
e: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} =$ $\frac{v - v_0}{t}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Distance: the path length travelled, with no direction.

q: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is _____.
e: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is increasing. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Negative acceleration is usually called _____ or retardation.
e: Negative acceleration is usually called deceleration or retardation. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: Motion along a straight line is called _____ motion.
e: Motion along a straight line is called linear motion. Linear names motion along a straight line. Circular: a round path, which is not the uniform-medium light path.

q: In linear motion with constant velocity, the acceleration is _____.
e: In linear motion with constant velocity, the acceleration is zero. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is $v =$ _____.
e: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is $v =$ $\frac{s}{t}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be _____.
e: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The first equation of motion for constant acceleration is $v =$ _____.
e: The first equation of motion for constant acceleration is $v =$ $v_0 + at$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and _____.
e: The equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Time: the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force.

q: The equation for displacement in constant acceleration motion is $s =$ _____.
e: The equation for displacement in constant acceleration motion is $s =$ $v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The average velocity $\bar{v}$ in constant acceleration motion is given by $\bar{v} =$ _____.
e: The average velocity $\bar{v}$ in constant acceleration motion is given by $\bar{v} =$ $\frac{v_0 + v}{2}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: In the MKS/SI system, the unit of displacement is _____.
e: In the MKS/SI system, the unit of displacement is m. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of velocity is _____.
e: In the CGS system, the unit of velocity is cm s$^{-1}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: In the FPS system, the unit of acceleration is _____.
e: In the FPS system, the unit of acceleration is ft s$^{-2}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The unit m s$^{-1}$ is read as _____.
e: The unit m s$^{-1}$ is read as metre per second. The physics in this sentence is built around metre per second.

q: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is _____ to the distance moved.
e: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is equal to the distance moved. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the _____.
e: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the same. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: In the equations of motion, we will use positive (+) and negative (-) signs to describe the two _____ directions along a straight line.
e: In the equations of motion, we will use positive (+) and negative (-) signs to describe the two opposite directions along a straight line. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite.

q: Except Eq. (2.7), the rest equations of motion can be expressed in _____ form.
e: Except Eq. (2.7), the rest equations of motion can be expressed in vector form. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.
Eq. (2.7) and Eq. (2.8) are derived from Eqs. (2.6), (2.9) and (2.10).

q: The instantaneous acceleration $a$ is defined as $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =$ _____.
e: The instantaneous acceleration $a$ is defined as $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =$ $\frac{dv}{dt}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: A body moving with a constant acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ changes its velocity by _____ in every second.
e: A body moving with a constant acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ changes its velocity by 5 m s$^{-1}$ in every second. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The speedometer of a car indicates the _____ speed of the car.
e: The speedometer of a car indicates the instantaneous speed of the car. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain _____.
e: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: Motion can be described or analyzed conveniently with the help of graphs. The motion graphs are of _____ types.
e: Motion can be described or analyzed conveniently with the help of graphs. The motion graphs are of three types. The physics in this sentence is built around three.

q: The three types of motion graphs are displacement-time graph, velocity-time graph, and _____ graph.
e: The three types of motion graphs are displacement-time graph, velocity-time graph, and acceleration-time graph. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The slope of the s-t graph gives the _____.
e: The slope of the s-t graph gives the velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: The slope of a v-t graph gives the _____ of a body.
e: The slope of a v-t graph gives the acceleration of a body. Acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Displacement: the straight directed change from start point to end point.

q: The area under a v-t graph gives the _____ (or) distance moved by the body.
e: The area under a v-t graph gives the displacement (or) distance moved by the body. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.
